endorsements.title: Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use
endorsements.quote: Clinicians should be a ware of the risks of patients engaging with generative AI products that produce inaccurate or harmful medical information (e.g., patients asking chatbots about symptoms) and should be prepared to counsel patients on the limitations of AI-driven medical advice.

endorsements.title: Data Science as a Core Competency in Undergraduate Medical Education in the Age of Artificial Intelligence in Health Care
endorsements.quote: Similar to how the advent of diagnostic imaging required the physician to understand, interpret, and explain the relevant results to patients, physicians of the future should be able to explain to patients the benefits and limitations of management plans guided by artificial intelligence.

endorsements.title: From Apomediation to AImediation: Generative AI and the Reconfiguration of Informational Authority in Health Communication
endorsements.issuer: Journal of primary care & community health
endorsements.quote: This reconfiguration of informational authority has profound implications for both patients and healthcare professionals.

endorsements.title: When the therapist hallucinates: AI, psychedelics, and the risks of unsupervised digital mental health care
endorsements.quote: As part of the discussion, when relevant, doctors should educate patients on the limitations of AI tools.

endorsements.title: Drone-delivered automated external defibrillators in prehospital emergency care: implementation evidence, bottlenecks, and conceptual integration with artificial intelligence and next-generation communications
endorsements.quote: Emergency departments and public-health programs should deliver CPR and AED training that includes drone-delivery scenarios.

evidence.title: Evaluation of performance of generative large language models for stroke care
evidence.effect: Most scores were below competency threshold 60; scores exceeding it typically reached only 60 to 65.
evidence.quote: Most scores fell below the minimum clinical competency threshold of 60, and even when LLMs exceeded this benchmark, the gains were marginal, typically only reaching 60 to 65 at most.

commentary.bottom_line: No study tests whether preparing physicians to counsel patients about consumer generative AI changes what patients do or reduces harm from inaccurate AI advice. The only supplied study documents the hazard: a simulation of five stroke questions found that most chatbot answers scored below a competency threshold of 60.

perspectives.view: Five sources endorse the practice. One is a guidance document and four are commentaries, and none reports outcome data. No study tests counseling or physician preparation. The single hazard study is a level 4 offline simulation of five questions in Taiwan. It shows that a problem exists and cannot show that counseling solves it, so certainty is rated as no direct evidence.

In the hazard study, most chatbot scores for patient-facing stroke advice fell below 60, and scores above that threshold typically reached only 60 to 65. Stroke care is time-sensitive, so poor advice may delay treatment. Counseling acts only when a patient reaches a clinician, and no data show whether it catches errors before patients act on them.

The one hazard study used five questions in an offline setting and reported no patient population. It gives no information on how Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients use chatbots or respond to physician counseling.

commentary.research_gap: Trials or controlled implementation studies should test whether physician training in AI counseling changes patient reliance on chatbot advice, time to appropriate care, and harm events. They should also measure the effect on visit time and clinician workload.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, and the hazard study did not include Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems therefore have no evidence on whether counseling reaches or helps these patients.
